newsitem.title: USA: General Signal sees earnings drop, stock falls.
newsitem.headline: General Signal sees earnings drop, stock falls.

text.p: General Signal, a maker of industrial equipment, said Wednesday that it expected lower earnings for the first quarter, disappointing investors and triggering a sell-off in its stock.
General Signal stock fell $2.625 to $41 after dipping as low as $38.50 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was one of the most active issues in late morning trading.
The Stamford, Conn.-based company said it expects earnings before taxes and other items to fall about 7 percent in the first quarter because of lower orders, sales and cost pressures.
General Signal earned $25.4 million, or 51 cents a share, on revenues of $481.7 million in the 1996 quarter, including a gain equal to 1 cent a share from the sale of a business unit.
Analysts had forecast earnings of 53 cents a share on average for the 1997 quarter, according to the company.
General Signal attributed the shortfall to the company's businesses in uninterruptible power supply equipment which protects computers from power outages, fire systems and pumps.
Initiatives have already been taken to bring costs in line with future revenue expectations, General Signal said.
"As a result of these corrective actions, we are optimistic that the company can still bring the full year into line with "Street" expectations," said Chairman Michael Lockhart.
General Signal, with 1996 sales of $2.07 billion, is a leading maker of products for process control, electrical control and industrial technology.
